_comment: Hand-authored rules for LCD L33822, version effective 01/01/2020 through 07/17/2021. Every source_sentence is verbatim from the PDF and is verified by exact search at load time. This file does double duty: it is the gold standard the LLM extraction is scored against, and it is the fallback ruleset so the pipeline runs end to end with no API key.
authored_by: human, by hand, reading the coverage criteria directly

rules.title: Diabetes mellitus diagnosis required
rules.summary: A therapeutic CGM requires a diabetes mellitus diagnosis.
rules.source_sentence: The beneficiary has diabetes mellitus (Refer to the ICD-10 code list in the LCD-related Policy Article for applicable diagnoses); and,

rules.title: Requires 4+ daily BGM testing
rules.summary: The beneficiary must already be testing with a blood glucose monitor four or more times a day.
rules.source_sentence: The beneficiary has been using a BGM and performing frequent (four or more times a day) testing; and,
rules._note: The 07/18/2021 revision deleted this criterion outright. Do not edit it here. The drift detector is supposed to discover that on its own.

rules.title: Insulin treatment threshold
rules.summary: Requires three or more daily insulin injections, or a Medicare-covered CSII pump.
rules.source_sentence: The beneficiary is insulin-treated with multiple (three or more) daily injections of insulin or a Medicare-covered continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion (CSII) pump; and,
rules._note: The 07/18/2021 revision changed this criterion twice: injections became administrations, and 'Medicare-covered' was dropped from the pump language.

rules.title: Regimen requires frequent adjustment
rules.summary: The insulin regimen must require frequent adjustment based on glucose testing results.
rules.source_sentence: The beneficiary's insulin treatment regimen requires frequent adjustment by the beneficiary on the basis of BGM or CGM testing results; and,

rules.title: In-person visit within 6 months prior to order
rules.summary: The treating practitioner must have seen the beneficiary in person within six months before ordering.
rules.source_sentence: Within six (6) months prior to ordering the CGM, the treating practitioner has an in-person visit with the beneficiary to evaluate their diabetes control and determined that criteria (1-4) above are met; and,
rules._note: The cited sentence contains the cross-reference 'criteria (1-4)', which the 2021 revision renumbered to '(1-3)'. That renumbering is not a coverage change and must not be flagged as one.

rules.title: Six-month follow-up visit
rules.summary: An in-person follow-up visit is required every six months after the initial prescription.
rules.source_sentence: Every six (6) months following the initial prescription of the CGM, the treating practitioner has an in-person visit with the beneficiary to assess adherence to their CGM regimen and diabetes treatment plan.

rules.title: Supply allowance limited to one unit per 30 days
rules.summary: Billing more than one unit of K0553 per 30 days is denied.
rules.source_sentence: Billing more than 1 UOS per 30 days of code K0553 will be denied as not reasonable and necessary.

rules.title: Home BGM requires a diabetes diagnosis
rules.summary: A home blood glucose monitor requires a diabetes diagnosis.
rules.source_sentence: The beneficiary has diabetes (Refer to the ICD-10 code list in the LCD-related Policy Article for applicable diagnoses); and

rules.title: Sufficient training evidenced by a prescription
rules.summary: The practitioner must have concluded the beneficiary has sufficient training, evidenced by a prescription.
rules.source_sentence: The beneficiary's treating practitioner has concluded that the beneficiary (or the beneficiary's caregiver) has sufficient training using the particular device prescribed as evidenced by providing a prescription for the appropriate supplies and frequency of blood glucose testing.

rules.title: Special-feature monitors require severe visual impairment
rules.summary: E2100 and E2101 require a certified severe visual impairment.
rules.source_sentence: Home blood glucose monitors with special features (HCPCS codes E2100, E2101) are covered when the basic coverage criteria (1)-(2) are met and the treating practitioner certifies that the beneficiary has a severe visual impairment (i.e., best corrected visual acuity of 20/200 or worse in both eyes) requiring use of this special monitoring system.

rules.title: Manual dexterity impairment for E2101
rules.summary: E2101 is also covered for impairment of manual dexterity severe enough to require the device.
rules.source_sentence: Code E2101 is also covered for those with impairment of manual dexterity when the basic coverage criteria (1)-(2) are met and the treating practitioner certifies that the beneficiary has an impairment of manual dexterity severe enough to require the use of this special monitoring system.
rules._note: Marked non-codifiable. 'Severe enough to require the use of this special monitoring system' is a clinical judgment the claim record cannot settle, so this always routes to a human and never auto-denies.

rules.title: Standard Written Order required before billing
rules.summary: A completed Standard Written Order must be received before the claim is submitted.
rules.source_sentence: If the supplier bills for an item addressed in this policy without first receiving a completed SWO, the claim shall be denied as not reasonable and necessary.
